Definition: to be (causatively, make) sharp or (figuratively) severe
BiblicalUsage: Chadad means to be sharp, to make sharp, or to be fierce. Iron sharpens iron and a man sharpens his friend, the sword of the LORD is sharpened to make a sore slaughter, and the horses of the Chaldeans are more fierce than the evening wolves.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sharpening is either friendship or judgment, and the edge is the same. Iron sharpens iron for good, and the sword is sharpened for slaughter — the difference is whose hand holds it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
